text: Declines happen. How you handle them decides whether the family leaves confused, or charged twice.
Tom Chen's saved card is on file for Biscuit's exam.
If a card is declined, don't keep trying it.
Click Card on file to charge it.
Scout says the card was declined.
Check the bill. The total is seventy five dollars, and nothing is paid.
Tell Tom kindly, and ask for another card.
In the field, you'll usually take a new card with Tap to Pay on the Stripe reader.
This demo has no reader connected, so we'll use Card over phone. It works the same way.
Click Card over phone to take the new card.
Type the name on the card.
Tom reads out the card number.
The expiry.
The security code.
And the ZIP.
Click Charge, once.
This card is declined too. If a card you type in is declined, the message says to check the number. Check the number once, with Tom.
He misread a digit. Click Cancel, and start the card again. If it's declined again, ask for another card.
Click Card over phone.
The name on the card.
This time, the right card number.
The expiry.
The security code.
And the ZIP.
Click Charge, once.
Scout says the card was charged and the invoice is paid.
The old decline message is gone, and the bill shows paid.
If the family can't pay today, leave the bill open and send a pay link. That's in the pay links video.

The most common mistakes are trying the same card again and again, and taking a second card before checking the first wasn't charged. Remember: don't retry again and again. Check the invoice, then ask for another card.
